newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Rising call rates push Sri Lanka rupee up vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Rising call rates push Sri Lanka rupee up vs dlr.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed slightly higher on Friday as rising call money rates prompted banks to shed dollars in exchange for the local currency, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.33 against the greenback after opening at 58.38. On Thursday, it closed at 58.40.
"With money rates going up, banks started to sell dollars to generate rupees," said an American Express dealer.
Money rates rose as a state name began borrowing and as one of the market's traditional big lenders remained on the sidelines, the American Express dealer said.
Call money, which opened at 7.5 percent, closed at 14 percent on increased demand ahead of this month's Sinhala and Tamil New Year, dealers said.
"It takes time for money to come into the system. Traditionally rates tend to go up a little during festive seasons," said a dealer who wished to remain unidentified.
The Central Bank left the exchange rate unchanged while its buying and selling prices also remained at Thursday's level of 57.5264 and 58.6886.
